title: Graph Neural Networks
overview: Graph neural networks learn from nodes and edges by passing messages between neighbors. They suit molecules, social networks and other relational data.
objectives: Implement one round of message passing

method.title: Message passing
method.body: Each node aggregates features from its neighbors, then updates its own representation.

method.title: GCN layer
method.body: H' = act(A_hat H W), where A_hat is the adjacency matrix with self-loops, degree-normalized.

method.title: Depth
method.body: Stacking k layers lets information travel k hops, but too many layers make node features indistinguishable (over-smoothing).

method.title: Readout
method.body: Graph-level tasks pool node embeddings into one vector by sum, mean or attention.

pseudocode:
A_hat = D^-1/2 (A + I) D^-1/2
H = relu(A_hat @ H @ W)
# graph readout
g = mean(H, axis=0)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
A = np.array([[0,1,0],[1,0,1],[0,1,0]], dtype=float)  # path graph 0-1-2
A_hat = A + np.eye(3)
d = A_hat.sum(1)
A_norm = A_hat / np.sqrt(np.outer(d, d))
H = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]])
W = np.eye(2)
H1 = np.maximum(0, A_norm @ H @ W)
print(np.round(H1, 3))
